body:
I don't have full knowledge about this area but probably this is the expected behavior as the `Window` will handle the input by itself and not repass them for the editor. A workaround you can try is add a script in the created window to manually repass the input for the editor `Window`:

```
@tool
extends Window

func _unhandled_key_input(event: InputEvent) -> void:
	get_tree().root.push_input(event)
```

And in your plugin script:

```
window = Window.new()
window.size = Vector2(500, 500)
window.title = "Shortcuts Don't Work Here"
window.set_script(preload("script_path"))
add_child(window)
```

I now realize the menu is part of the other window, and having the new window stop the inputs makes perfect sense.  It's confusing, at least on Mac, because the menu bar is not part of the window itself, and it doesn't change when the new window has focus.

Adding the `_unhandled_key_input` you suggested does work, but opens up a different can of worms.  For example, `ctrl/cmd + w` now closes the currently opened script in the editor when the user would expect it to close the window.  Before adding `_unhandled_key_input` it just did nothing, which is better than closing the wrong thing. 

Since I know all my shortcuts, I tried only passing known keystrokes to the editor vial `_unhandled_key_input`.  This seems to work well.  

Is it possible to get shortcuts defined in the editor.  I would really like to be able to get the shortcut defined for "Script Editor->Close" and use that to close my window.  This would also allow me to "punch through" any editor shortcuts that make sense. If so, is there also a way to be notified when editor shortcuts are changed?  I was unable to find any documentation about this.
